html:
Zoroaster, or Zarathustra, was an Iranian prophet and poet, the founder of Zoroastrianism. When and where he lived is unknown. Tradition dates him to the 7th and 6th centuries BCE, but the language of his hymns suggests to many scholars a much earlier date, perhaps around 1000 BCE or before, somewhere in eastern Iran or Central Asia, perhaps Bactria.

His teachings survive in the Gathas, seventeen hymns in old Avestan that form the oldest part of the Avesta. He preached one supreme wise god, Ahura Mazda, and a world split between truth and the lie, good and evil. Each person must choose a side, and will be judged.

His faith became the religion of the Persian kings of the Achaemenid and Sasanian empires. After the Arab conquest of Iran it slowly shrank. Some believers fled to India, where their descendants, the Parsis, still live, as told in Zoroastrians settle in Gujarat.

Many scholars think his ideas of heaven and hell, a final judgment and a saviour to come influenced Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
